official.deadline_note: There are no application deadlines - applications are accepted all year and enter one of two evaluation rounds. The next hard cutoff is Friday 22 January 2027, 14:00 CET (Spring round, fourth Friday of January; results around mid-June). The second cutoff is the second Friday of July, 14:00 CEST (Autumn round; results around mid-December). Applications completed after 14:00 CE(S)T on a cutoff day enter the next round - no exceptions.
official.application_cycle: Rolling applications; two evaluation rounds per year (Spring round cutoff: fourth Friday of January, 14:00 CET; Autumn round cutoff: second Friday of July, 14:00 CEST)
official.status_note: Applications accepted throughout the year; the site banner states the next cutoff date - hard deadline: Friday 22 January 2027, 14:00 CET.
official.tuition_coverage_note: EMBO publishes no tuition support: in EMBC Member States the grant funds only a host-institution employment contract (social contributions, taxes and net salary of the fellow), and elsewhere the stipend is solely intended to cover the cost of living in the host country. Bench fees, overheads, consumables and any other financial benefits to the host supervisor or receiving institute are explicitly not covered.
benefits: Salary or stipend for the postdoctoral position: in EMBC Member States a grant-funded host employment contract (2026 yearly grant rates EUR 51,600-99,600 depending on country); elsewhere a yearly stipend (US EUR 65,400; Singapore EUR 63,600; Japan EUR 60,000; Canada EUR 46,800; Australia EUR 51,000; Taiwan EUR 51,000; India EUR 39,600; Chile EUR 28,200)

Travel and relocation allowance paid as a lump sum, ideally before the fellowship start: travel EUR 200-750 by distance tier plus relocation EUR 1,020-2,100 by destination country, plus up to EUR 2,000 for travel of the fellow's partner and children
Child daycare allowance up to EUR 2,500 per fellowship year per child for children under six (non-EMBC fellows), prorated and reimbursed after the first fellowship year
Country-specific additional allowance for each dependent child under 18 (non-EMBC fellows; e.g. US EUR 9,810, Singapore EUR 9,200, Japan EUR 9,000 per year)

Free attendance at an online EMBO Laboratory Leadership Course and one 1-day Scientific Skills course within three years of the award; access to the EMBO Fellows' Network and the annual Fellows' Meeting
Parental leave support: EMBC-based fellows can extend the fellowship at no cost to EMBO; non-EMBC fellows receive three months paid parental leave with an equivalent extension
eligibility: Applicants must hold a PhD or equivalent at the start of the fellowship; those who already hold a PhD are eligible only if it was obtained within the two years preceding the application submission date

At least one first (or joint first) author primary research paper accepted for publication or published in an international peer-reviewed journal at the time of application; a first-author preprint with public in-depth peer reviews verifiably obtained from an independent service (e.g. Review Commons, Peer Community In) also qualifies

All applications must involve movement between countries; applications to the country where the PhD was obtained, to the laboratory, institute or department where the PhD was done, or again with the PhD supervisor, will not be considered

Applications to return to a laboratory where the candidate worked for more than six months in total (including master's studies) are not eligible; candidates already in the host laboratory may apply only if they have lived in the host country for less than six months at submission
For hosts outside EMBC Member States (maximum 30% of fellowships): the applicant must be a national of an EMBC Member State, have performed their PhD in one, and be moving from one

The research proposal must fall within EMBO's scientific scope and must not be a direct continuation of the PhD project; one application per candidate per round for one project at one host laboratory; re-application currently permitted only once (re-applications end for applications submitted after 22 January 2027, 14:00 CET)
requirements: Online application written in English via the EMBO application system; text only - no figures, tables or special formatting

Two reference letters submitted through the online system: one must come from the PhD supervisor or PhD co-supervisor, and none may come from referees at the receiving institute; institutional (not private) email addresses are required
Acceptance letter from the receiving institute submitted through the same system
CV and list of publications, without journal impact factors or any other journal-based metrics (EMBO is a DORA signatory)
Confirmed host supervisor and host laboratory, with agreement that the EMBO grant is used to fund the fellow's employment contract (EMBC Member States)
For papers 'accepted' or 'accepted in principle' but not yet published, the editorial letter proving first-author status must be emailed to fellowships@embo.org before submitting the application
documents: Completed online application form (English, text only) confirmed as complete in the system
Two reference letters submitted online (one from the PhD supervisor/co-supervisor; none from the receiving institute)
Acceptance letter from the receiving institute submitted online
Editorial acceptance letter emailed to the Fellowship Office for accepted-but-unpublished first-author papers
Documentation of any claimed career-break exception (e.g. parental leave, military service), approved by the Fellowship Office before submission
selection_criteria: Primary criteria: scientific excellence of the candidate, of the project and of the host laboratory
Scientific achievements of the applicant (contributions and CV; performance based on reference letters)
Project proposal: quality, scope, novelty and biological significance, plus coherent and logical presentation
Host laboratory: suitability for the proposed research and training, and its scientific achievements - applications to labs the candidate has previously collaborated with receive lower priority

Three-stage evaluation: office pre-screening (top ~20-25% ranked applications proceed), a 90-minute online interview with a presentation, then independent evaluation and a final decision by the EMBO Fellowship Committee; outcome typically 16-18 weeks after the cutoff
No individual feedback is provided at any stage; roughly 1,000 applications are received per round with a success rate of about 8%
coverage: In EMBC Member States: a yearly grant transferred to the host institution to cover a full-time employment contract for the fellow, including employer's and awardee's social contributions, taxes and the net salary (2026 rates EUR 51,600 per year in most states, up to EUR 99,600 in Iceland; the net salary will be lower than the grant rate)

Outside EMBC Member States: a yearly stipend solely intended to cover the cost of living in the host country (US EUR 65,400; Singapore EUR 63,600; Japan EUR 60,000; Taiwan EUR 51,000; Australia EUR 51,000; Canada EUR 46,800; India EUR 39,600; Chile EUR 28,200), which may be taxable

Travel and relocation allowance as a lump sum: travel EUR 200-750 by approximate distance tier, relocation EUR 1,020-2,100 by destination country, and up to EUR 2,000 extra for partner and children's travel
Child daycare up to EUR 2,500 per fellowship year per child (children under six, non-EMBC fellows) plus a country-specific dependent-child allowance for children under 18
Free online Laboratory Leadership and Scientific Skills courses, Fellows' Network and Fellows' Meeting access; fellowship extension for parental, maternity or long-term sick leave
Explicitly not covered: bench fees, overheads, funds for consumables or any other financial benefits to the host supervisor or receiving institute
application_method: Register for an account in the EMBO online application system (applications.embo.org) and complete the application online
Have both referees and the receiving institute submit their letters through the same system before completion - registration alone does not enter an evaluation round
Confirm completion and submit before the 14:00 CE(S)T cutoff of the intended round; applications completed after the cutoff enter the next round
official.application_route: Apply only through the EMBO online application system: register, complete the English text-only form, have two referees (one being the PhD supervisor) and the host institute upload their letters, then confirm completion before the 14:00 CE(S)T cutoff.
official.study_mode: Full-time; part-time work at 50% or 75% is possible on request at no cost to EMBO, with combined full-time and part-time duration capped at 36 months
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality restriction for fellowships in EMBC Member States (international mobility required). For EMBC/EMBO global partners (Chile, India, Singapore, Taiwan) the applicant must move from and be a national of an EMBC Member State or global partner and have done the PhD there; for other non-EMBC countries (capped at 30% of awards) the applicant must be an EMBC Member State national, have performed the PhD in one and be moving from one.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - applicants of any nationality may apply to work in an EMBC Member State provided there is international mobility; destinations outside EMBC Member States are restricted to the mobility and nationality rules above.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Research proposals must fall within EMBO's scientific scope in the life sciences (subject areas include Cell Cycle; Cell & Tissue Architecture; Cellular Metabolism; Chromatin & Transcription; Development, Differentiation & Death; Evolution & Ecology; Genome Stability & Dynamics; Genomic & Computational Biology; Immunology; Membranes & Transport; Microbiology, Virology & Pathogens; Molecular Medicine; Neuroscience; Plant Biology; Proteins & Biochemistry; RNA; Signal Transduction; Structural Biology & Biophysics; Systems Biology). Applied or clinical work without a clear biological question is not eligible, and applications to industrial laboratories aimed at commercial products are not considered.
official.research_requirement: A research proposal for a postdoctoral project that is not a direct continuation of the PhD work, driven by a biological question and expected to yield mechanistic biological insight; the proposal must be submitted as text only, without figures or tables.
official.duration: Awarded for up to two years (24 months); shorter durations can be requested with a minimum of 12 months; full-time plus part-time duration must not exceed 36 months; fellowships must start within one calendar year of the relevant evaluation cutoff and can only begin on the 1st or 15th of a month.
official.description: EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships support excellent postdoctoral researchers throughout Europe and the world for a period of up to two years, with international mobility a key requirement. The fellowship includes a salary or stipend, a relocation allowance and support for fellows with children. Awardees also attend an EMBO Laboratory Leadership course free of charge and become part of the global network of EMBO Fellows.
official.region: Europe and worldwide: EMBC Member States, EMBC/EMBO global partners (Chile, India, Singapore, Taiwan) and non-EMBC Member States
official.english_requirement: Applications must be written in English; no IELTS, TOEFL or other English test score is required or published.

not_confirmed: tuition_coverage - EMBO publishes no tuition support for this postdoctoral scheme (only salary/stipend, travel/relocation and family allowances)

A single headline amount - the published 2026 rate is country-specific (EUR 51,600-99,600 per year grant in EMBC Member States; EUR 28,200-65,400 per year stipend elsewhere), so funding_amount records the lowest published yearly rate and the full range is given in coverage/benefits
verification.notes: All figures taken from EMBO's own pages: the 2026 contract/stipend rate sheet, the July 2026 application guidelines PDF, the June 2026 travel and relocation policy PDF, and the fellowship overview, benefits, eligibility, application and FAQ pages. No aggregator sources were used.

applicant_utility.summary: This scheme pays a real salary through the host institution in most of Europe, so the money you see on the rate sheet is a gross grant, not your net pay - talk to your prospective host about the actual contract value before you commit. Because applications roll continuously into two cutoffs a year, the practical deadline is whenever your host lab, both referees and your PhD supervisor can all deliver their letters through the portal, which usually takes weeks of lead time. The two strictest gates are the two-year clock from your PhD award date and the ban on returning to your PhD country, lab or supervisor, so map your mobility history against those rules before you invest in a proposal. Expect roughly a 1-in-12 chance per round and no feedback if you miss, so treat this as one arm of a wider postdoc search rather than a single bet.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Life-science researchers within two years of their PhD award who hold a first-author paper, can secure a genuinely new host laboratory in another country, and want a salaried, mobile postdoc.
application_readiness_checklist: Email fellowships@embo.org before applying if your PhD award date is close to the two-year limit or you had parental leave, military service or illness, and get the exception approved in writing first
Line up the host lab early and confirm in writing that the institute will issue an employment contract (EMBC states) and that the grant rate for that country is acceptable
Brief both referees months ahead - one must be your PhD supervisor or co-supervisor, and neither may sit at the receiving institute; the portal blocks submission until their letters arrive
Ask each accepted-but-unpublished first-author paper's journal for the editorial acceptance letter and send it to fellowships@embo.org before you submit
Draft the proposal as plain text with no figures or tables, and strip journal impact factors from your publication list
common_rejection_risks: A proposal that reads as a continuation of the PhD project - this is an explicit eligibility bar, not just a scoring weakness
Missing the two-year window since PhD award at the moment of submission, or assuming the cutoff date rather than your actual submission date counts
Any prior stay over six months in the host country, or working in the chosen lab before, without checking the mobility rules
No first-author primary research paper with verifiable peer review - submitted, in-preparation or review papers do not count
Submitting with incomplete reference or acceptance letters, or registering an account but never confirming completion before the 14:00 CE(S)T cutoff
Reapplying with a barely changed application - copies of the previous proposal are rejected immediately, and reapplication ends altogether for applications after 22 January 2027
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Bench fees, consumables, lab overheads and any institutional charges are excluded from the grant, so the host lab must cover research costs from its own funds or other grants. The grant rate is not your net salary - taxes and social contributions come out of it, and if the host caps salaries below the EMBO rate the difference returns to EMBO. Fellows outside EMBC Member States arrange their own tax, visa, insurance and relocation logistics; the travel and relocation lump sum (EUR 1,220-2,850 typical range) will rarely cover a full international move, and it must be repaid in full if the fellowship ends within six months.
document_audit: Reference letters must arrive through the online portal from institutional email addresses - letters sent by email or from personal accounts are simply not considered

For an accepted-but-unpublished first-author paper, the editorial letter must prove your first-author status and must be emailed before submission; publication updates after submission force a re-open and can reset your submission date
The receiving institute's acceptance letter is a separate mandatory submission - confirm the institute director or authorised signatory can sign the EMBO-host grant agreement later
If you claim a career-break exception, the supporting documentation must already be approved by the Fellowship Office before you apply; applications without prior approval are deemed ineligible
Add a disclosure of any AI tools used in preparing the application, as EMBO now requests this
alerts: From the Autumn 2027 round (applications after 22 January 2027, 14:00 CET) re-applications are no longer permitted - you get one EMBO fellowship proposal ever, so timing matters more than in past cycles

Since the Autumn 2026 round a host laboratory may support only one candidate per selection round; if you and a lab-mate both apply to the same lab, EMBO will ask the lab to withdraw the extra applications
The submission timestamp in Central European Time is what counts for eligibility checks - an application completed minutes after 14:00 CET on a cutoff day silently rolls into the next round

Fellowships can only start on the 1st or 15th of a month, within one calendar year of the cutoff (Spring awardees: July of the award year to 15 February of the next; Autumn awardees: 1 January to 15 August), so align your current contract end date accordingly
If you are awarded other funding mid-evaluation you must tell the Fellowship Office whether you still want to be considered, otherwise you risk losing the award or holding it unfunded
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register online, fill in the English text-only form, trigger the two referee forms and the host acceptance letter inside the portal, wait for all letters to land, then confirm completion - the application is only 'in' once every component is submitted and confirmed before the 14:00 CE(S)T cutoff.
